title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
content_md: South Korean police identified seven suspects linked to a cybercrime operation that breached more than 90 organizations in the country, with ARTEX AI pentesting framework used in most of the attacks. According to local media citing the Seoul Metropolitan Police, the gang leader has a background in penetration testing and worked at a cybersecurity company between 2019 and 2022. In 38 of the incidents, the threat actor demanded ransom payments of 360 million won ($270,000), promising in exchange not to leak stolen data. Authorities believe the threat actor stole 8.2 million records from compromised organizations, including educational institutes, hospitals, large corporations, and even golf courses. Yonhap News says that the gang leader is a self-taught 32 year-old hacker and started attacking organizations in September 2025. The Seoul Metropolitan police told the publication that the hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite, the same autonomous framework used in the attacks against multiple South Korean banks attributed to a Chinese-speaking threat actor. Initially, the hacker used conventional tools but adopted AI utilities in late August 2026 to expand the attacks. Authorities arrested all seven suspects, but only the group’s leader remains in custody. Arrested on October 15, he was formally detained two days later and referred to prosecutors on October 23.
